question: Reference distances were not measured on the partitioned path at all. Can they be, without paying the cross-partition n^2 the partitioning exists to avoid -- and do they agree with the monolithic pass?
answer: Yes to both, and the per-partition pass is MORE accurate. Identical coverage (22,151 pairs), zero disagreement on every pair below distance 0.7, and the single pair that crosses the 0.3 cutoff is one the monolithic pass got wrong: a GCF-22 member with an IDENTICAL domain set to the pantaphos reference (jaccard 1.0) that the monolithic run scored 0.894. The pantaphos family reads 186 of 186 within cutoff instead of 185 of 186.
why_not_post_merge: BiG-SCAPE's PartialRecordPairGenerator (comparison/binning.py) yields exactly the pairs ABSENT from the distance table for the matching edge_param_id. A merged partition database is missing precisely the cross-partition query pairs, so a reference pass over it computes all of them -- ~34 M at a 2-way split of 11,700 BGCs against the ~199 k wanted. merge_bigscape_dbs.py deduplicates edge_params rather than offsetting them, so within-partition distances keep a valid edge_param_id and really are skipped; the cross-partition ones really are not.
design: Per partition, inside BIGSCAPE_PARTITION, after the clean pass and on a COPY of that partition's database. Each partition database is already complete within itself, so adding references costs refs x partition size, summing over partitions to exactly the refs x N a monolithic pass does. It lives in that process rather than its own because the input is already staged and already laid out as part_input/<genome>/.

measured.input: 1,303 Enterobacterales region GenBanks from the RefSeq run, 1,261 distinct genomes, 17 characterised references

the_disagreements_are_all_among_non_hits.reading: Nothing below 0.7 moves at all. Every difference sits among pairs that share almost nothing, which is where BiG-SCAPE's documented order-dependence lives -- load order decides each pair's A/B orientation and the extended comparison is not symmetric under it. A prediction of 'third-decimal jitter' made before the test was wrong in magnitude (median 0.015, max 0.73) and right in location.

the_one_pair_that_crosses_the_cutoff.which_is_right: The per-partition one. The region is a member of the pantaphos family (GCF-22, 186 members), and jaccard 1.0 means its domain set is IDENTICAL to the reference's -- a distance of 0.894 for that is not credible. The monolithic load order oriented the pair so the extended comparison found no common subsequence and fell back to a near-empty one.
the_one_pair_that_crosses_the_cutoff.consequence: The pantaphos family reads 186 of 186 within cutoff rather than 185 of 186. The '185 of 186' previously noted as a curiosity was this artefact.

everything_else_reproduces.families_pantaphos_reaches: 186/186 at 0.0, 28/28 at 0.0196, 21/21 at 0.199 -- the same three families and the same distances to 4 dp (family IDs differ, being per-run autoincrements)

code.reference_distances.py: --pass-db takes one or more databases and concatenates their rows. The family join moved from record_id to (genome, region): merge_bigscape_dbs.py offsets record ids per partition, so a partition's record 7 is not the merged database's record 7 and the id join would attach each distance to an unrelated family. Verified byte-identical to the published monolithic output on the unpartitioned path before any module change.
code.BIGSCAPE_PARTITION: gains the reference directory, its digest as a val input, and an optional refpass_<id>.db output. A run without references stages a placeholder file, the -d guard fails, and no pass runs.
code.PARTITION_REFERENCE_DISTANCES: new; reads the per-partition databases plus the merged one. Runs no BiG-SCAPE.
code.clustering.nf: the log.warn is replaced by the real call; the monolithic BIGSCAPE_REFERENCES is now gated on !params.bigscape_partition.

test_harness_note: The first attempt pointed partition_bgcs.py at a FLAT directory of staged GBKs, which made every region report genome='all' -- genome_of() derives the genome from the path, which is why BIGSCAPE_PARTITION rebuilds part_input/<genome>/. The join key collapsed and the comparison found no shared pairs. Redone against the real antismash_input tree. Partitioning itself was unaffected (8 partitions, largest 943 against 942) because the cut keys on pepM sequence, not paths.
